humanAcceptance.evidence: After the exact immutable preview existed, Codex applied Dave's standing instruction in the active task: Pass 63 will be the next Live release; get it published. This records release authorization and does not claim a separate visual inspection of the newly generated artifact.

requirements.summary: Atomic Acres opaque-surface integrity and traversable house apertures
requirements.expected: Opaque house walls block selected practical-light and effect contribution, while entrances and upstairs apertures stay visibly open and collision-authoritative in both rendering profiles.
requirements.falsifier: A representative opaque wall exposes the audited light contribution, a black slab returns in an opening, or presentation and collision disagree.

evidence.note: The served Quality and Performance routes exercise the repaired apertures and representative light-occlusion contract.
The immutable Pass 63 preview contains the final Atomic presentation at the accepted source SHA.

requirements.summary: Skyline Terminal opening and collider parity
requirements.expected: Boarding routes, aircraft cabin openings, cockpit access, true glass, signs, and displays render consistently with movement and projectile authority in both profiles.
requirements.falsifier: An audited opening looks like a wall, an open route is blocked, glass becomes opaque, or a sign/display is made transparent.

evidence.note: The served matrix traverses and probes the audited Terminal openings in Performance and Quality.
The immutable preview is the final Pass 63 Terminal visual artifact.

requirements.expected: Lobby and match chat is host-validated, bounded, sanitized, ordered identically for peers, keyboard-safe, ephemeral, and excluded from diagnostics and external persistence.
requirements.falsifier: A guest can spoof identity or order, malformed text reaches peers, gameplay hotkeys fire while typing, or message text is persisted into diagnostics.

evidence.command: npx vitest run src/text-chat.test.ts src/text-chat-ui.test.ts src/protocol.test.ts src/network-lifecycle.test.ts
evidence.note: Covers host validation, wire bounds, sanitization, ordering, UI keyboard ownership, and lifecycle cleanup.
A real served peer session proves common chat delivery and lobby/match composer behavior.

requirements.summary: Accessible Project Map with canonical current-first exports
requirements.expected: The Project Map dialog exposes Overview, Structure, Changes, and Archive from one typed source and downloads safe Markdown and JSON with current architecture before complete history.
requirements.falsifier: A documented source path is missing, UI and exports diverge, history precedes current state, unsafe text is injected, or a tab/download is inaccessible.

evidence.command: npx vitest run src/project-map.test.ts src/ui/project-map-dialog.test.ts src/changelog.test.ts
evidence.note: Validates stable IDs, real repository paths, archive completeness, current-first ordering, and safe serialization.
Exercises all dialog tabs and both downloads in the served application.
The immutable preview contains the accessible Project Map presentation.

requirements.summary: Bounded recurring cleanup without gameplay-authority drift
requirements.expected: Menu documentation-dialog ownership is extracted, replaced wiring and proven unused symbols are removed, and remaining hotspots are measured without a broad tree move.
requirements.falsifier: Duplicate dialog lifecycle code remains active, TypeScript finds unused code, or the cleanup changes gameplay authority.

evidence.note: Strict TypeScript and the bounded specification keep the extraction scoped to real ownership boundaries.

requirements.summary: Pass 62 gameplay and accepted Rustworks contracts remain intact
requirements.expected: Host-authoritative shot timing, DHV, 2x Damage, corpse, redeploy, profile/collision behavior, and the accepted Rustworks layout remain unchanged.
requirements.falsifier: A core deterministic contract changes, Rustworks browser coverage regresses, or Quality and Performance disagree on gameplay authority.

evidence.note: The complete static, deterministic gameplay, provenance, unit, leaderboard, build, release-tree, and production dependency gates passed on the immutable source SHA.
The accepted one-ramp and 8/4/4 Rustworks composition remains in the Pass 63 browser gate.

requirements.summary: Pass 63 Live and byte-exact Pass 62 Stable release topology
requirements.expected: The root chooser exposes Pass 63 as Live and a pinned Pass 62 Stable subtree whose 118 runtime files retain the protected production digest and original provenance; legacy and room aliases enter Pass 63.
requirements.falsifier: Pass 62 is rebuilt from current source, any pinned byte differs, the protected digest changes, an extra channel appears, or a current alias enters anything except Pass 63.

evidence.command: npm run stage:release-topology && npm run verify:release-topology
evidence.note: Stages and byte-compares the protected nested Pass 62 Pages subtree while preserving its original provenance and adding pinned-channel provenance.
The chooser and latest, normal, and room aliases were exercised against the staged two-channel tree.

requirements.summary: Exact immutable Pass 63 candidate is authorized for publication
requirements.expected: The published runtime derives from the exact source SHA that produced the immutable preview and differs afterward only by this acceptance record and allowed process metadata.
requirements.falsifier: Runtime or release content changes after preview creation, the artifact source differs, or publication lacks Dave's direct authorization.

evidence.note: The exact candidate's staged chooser and all compatibility aliases were exercised before publication authorization was recorded.
Immutable GitHub Actions preview artifact 8613361053 was created from the exact accepted source SHA before authorization was recorded.
The gate enforces exact preview identity, post-preview approval ordering, requirement coverage, and preview-to-head parity.
